title: From Michelin Stars to Grocery Aisles: Gymkhana Brings Premium Indian Sauces to America
excerpt: The two-Michelin-starred London restaurant's CPG line launches in Whole Foods nationwide, backed by an $8.5 million Series A as Indian cuisine enters its premium moment in the US.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Gymkhana Fine Foods launches premium Indian sauces in Whole Foods, backed by $8.5 million funding.
  • The brand aims to elevate Indian cuisine in American grocery stores with restaurant-quality products.
  • Indian food now represents over $5 billion in at-home consumption in the US and UK.
  • Gymkhana's UK success includes over 1,000 retail locations and rapid growth in ambient sauces.
  • Indian cuisine is the second-fastest-growing global cuisine in America, signaling a premium moment.

> **""Gymkhana restaurant has proved that Indian cuisine belongs at the highest level of global dining," said Gulrez Singh Arora, co-founder and CEO of Gymkhana Fine Foods."** London's culinary elite has a new mission: your kitchen pantry. Gymkhana Fine Foods, the consumer packaged goods arm of London's two-Michelin-starred Gymkhana restaurant, has launched exclusively in Whole Foods Market stores across the United States. The move is backed by an $8.5 million Series A funding round led by CAVU Consumer Partners — the venture firm behind brands like Poppi, Bai, and Vital Proteins — and co-founded by Rohan Oza of "Shark Tank" fame. ## Restaurant Pedigree Meets the Grocery Shelf The brand is the brainchild of JKS Restaurants, the hospitality group founded by siblings Jyotin, Karam, and Sunaina Sethi. JKS's portfolio spans more than 30 Indian concepts across the UK, US, and Middle East, boasting eight Michelin stars and six Bib Gourmand mentions collectively. Gymkhana, their flagship, is widely regarded as one of the finest Indian restaurants in the world. "Gymkhana restaurant has proved that Indian cuisine belongs at the highest level of global dining," said Gulrez Singh Arora, co-founder and CEO of Gymkhana Fine Foods. "Now we're bringing that magic into every kitchen." The US debut features a lineup of simmer sauces — Butter Masala, Goan Coconut Curry, Korma, Tikka Masala, and Madras — alongside marinades like Classic Tandoori BBQ, Green Tikka, and Roasted Garlic & Chili. Each jar is priced between $8 and $10 and promises a restaurant-quality meal in under 30 minutes. ## A Market Ready for the Upgrade The timing is deliberate. Indian food now accounts for more than $5 billion in at-home consumption across the US and UK, yet the retail category has historically lacked a premium, restaurant-credentialed brand. In the UK, where Gymkhana Fine Foods launched in 2023, the brand has grown to over 1,000 doors across Whole Foods UK, Waitrose, and Sainsbury's — and Nielsen data shows it is the primary growth driver across ambient sauce brands in the UK over the past 26 weeks, outpacing Heinz and Mutti. The US launch follows the opening of Gymkhana's first American restaurant at the Aria Resort & Casino in Las Vegas, and the Sethi siblings' expansion of their Punjabi concept Ambassadors Clubhouse to New York. Indian cuisine, Dataessential reports, is now the second-fastest-growing global cuisine in America. ## What This Means for the Diaspora For NRIs who grew up watching Patak's and MDH dominate the Indian grocery aisle, Gymkhana's entry represents something different: a premium Indian brand that doesn't need to explain itself. It arrives with the cultural cachet of Michelin stars and the backing of mainstream venture capital — a signal that Indian cuisine is no longer niche, and no longer needs to be cheap to be accepted. "This isn't just a product launch," Arora says. "It's the beginning of Indian food's premium moment in America." ## What's Next With CAVU's Rohan Oza and Jared Jacobs on the board, Gymkhana Fine Foods has the playbook and the capital to scale beyond Whole Foods. The brand's trajectory in the UK — from launch to market leader in under three years — suggests the American chapter could move quickly. For diaspora families who have long served restaurant-quality Indian food at home, Gymkhana is essentially bottling what they already knew: that no other cuisine can match Indian flavors when the recipe is right.
